questions.question_text:
A person records a BAC of $0.06$.
Use $\text{Time} = \dfrac{\text{BAC}}{0.015}$ to calculate the number of hours required for their BAC to drop to zero.

options.why: Multiplied $0.06$ by $0.015$ instead of dividing.
Divided by $0.024$ instead of the standard rate $0.015$.
Divided by $0.01$ instead of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A driver tested at a roadside checkpoint records a BAC of $0.035$.
Calculate the time required for their BAC to reach zero, in hours and minutes.

options.why: Treated $0.333\ldots\text{ hours}$ as $33\text{ minutes}$ instead of multiplying by $60$.
Kept the $2$ whole hours from the quotient but used the BAC digits as $35$ minutes instead of converting the fractional hour.
Divided by $0.02$ instead of the standard metabolic rate of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A person has a BAC of $0.09$ when drinking stops.
Estimate how many hours they must wait for their BAC to drop to zero.

options.why: Multiplied $0.09$ by $0.015$ instead of dividing.
Divided $0.09$ by $0.01$ instead of $0.015$.
Divided $0.09$ by $0.02$ instead of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A $75\text{ kg}$ male consumes $5$ standard drinks over $3\text{ hours}$.
Calculate how long he must wait after drinking stops for his BAC to reach zero, to the nearest minute.

options.why: Used the female formula constant ($5.5$) instead of the male constant ($6.8$) to calculate BAC.
Calculated the total time from when drinking began instead of the waiting time after drinking stops.
Used $0.02$ as the hourly metabolic rate instead of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A person has a BAC of $0.065$ when drinking stops.
Estimate the waiting time for their BAC to drop to zero, in hours and minutes.

options.why: Treated $0.333\ldots\text{ hours}$ as $33\text{ minutes}$ instead of multiplying by $60$.
Divided $0.065$ by $0.01$ instead of $0.015$.
Divided $0.065$ by $0.02$ instead of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A person has a BAC of $0.072$.
Calculate the time required for their BAC to reach zero, in hours and minutes.

options.why: Treated $0.8$ hours as $8$ minutes instead of multiplying by $60$.
Rounded $4.8$ hours to $4.5$ hours.
Divided $0.078$ by $0.015$ due to a transcription error.

questions.question_text:
A person has a BAC of $0.063$ when drinking stops.
Estimate the waiting time for their BAC to drop to zero, in hours and minutes.

options.why: Treated $0.2\text{ hours}$ as $20\text{ minutes}$ instead of multiplying by $60$.
Divided $0.063$ by $0.01$ instead of $0.015$.
Divided $0.063$ by $0.02$ instead of $0.015$.

questions.question_text:
A $64\text{ kg}$ female drinks $5$ standard drinks over $2.5\text{ hours}$.
Estimate how long she must wait after drinking stops for her BAC to drop to zero. Answer in hours and minutes to the nearest minute.

options.why: Added the $2.5\text{ hours}$ of drinking to the waiting time after drinking stops.
Used the male formula constant $6.8$ instead of the female constant $5.5$.
Omitted the subtraction of $7.5H$ when calculating BAC.
